summary: Nora now stops cleanly when Docker stops her: a Cognition session in flight releases its unit instead of holding it for an hour.
details: SIGTERM and SIGINT now stop the process through its normal shutdown. Before, `docker stop` killed it on the spot, and a session in flight left its wake open, which held its unit for up to 3,900 s and then counted as a failed session. Now a running session gets 30 s to finish, then it is cancelled and recorded as a restart, and compose gives the service a 75 s stop grace. A second signal ends the process at once.

At boot, any wake a previous process left open is released the same way, so a kill that the grace did not cover no longer costs the unit its next hour or a failure count. A restart never strikes a stimulus.
A session's input, output and cache-read tokens and its trace id are now stored on its outcome row (migration 0090), so spend survives a restart.
limitations: Nora must be recreated for the stop grace to take effect.
There is still no dead-man switch: nothing says so if Prometheus, Alertmanager or the Discord bridge stops.
A tag turn in flight at a stop still ends with the process.
Nothing enforces one nora process per database apart from the fixed container name: a dev run pointed at the production database would cancel the live process's open wakes.
